question: how does a configurable product become a line item in the cart
answer: A configurable product becomes a line item through its own mutation, createConfiguredLineItem, which takes configurableProductId plus configurationSections (InputCreateConfiguredLineItemCommand) and is NOT the ordinary addItem path; the resulting LineItemType carries configurationItems. The base's two type tables answered the schema half correctly. The half it could not answer -- what the storefront actually does -- turned out to be unanswerable on this deployment: vcptcore_stable has no configurable product at all (POST /api/catalog/products/configurations/search returns totalCount 0 platform-wide).
found_via: kb deliver for the schema; POST /api/catalog/products/configurations/search and the storefront isConfigurable field for the absence
note: Answered as a type table, not as a procedure. Useful anyway because the input type names the route.

question: which REST route searches catalog products by product type
answer: There is no product-search route under /api/catalog/products at all -- the base's own table of its 26 operations shows create/read/patch/clone but nothing that searches. Product search on this platform is POST /api/catalog/listentries, which takes catalogId + searchInChildren + objectTypes and, decisively, searchInVariations: with it false you get 204 products in this store's catalog and with it true you get 259, so the difference is exactly the variation products.
found_via: the Admin SPA's own network calls showed listentries; the base confirmed the absence of a products/search route
note: The base answered by exhaustively listing what IS there, which is how I could tell what is not. A table that is complete is a usable negative answer.

question: which money fields does an order line item carry with and without tax
answer: OrderLineItemType carries the whole money family twice: price/priceWithTax, placedPrice/placedPriceWithTax, extendedPrice/extendedPriceWithTax, listTotal/listTotalWithTax, discountAmount/discountAmountWithTax, discountTotal/discountTotalWithTax, plus taxTotal and taxPercentRate. Verified against the live order: the REST record carries every one of them and on a zero-tax order each WithTax value equals its counterpart. The storefront's own order query selects only the non-tax half, which is the storefront's choice and not a schema gap.
note: Asked at the moment I needed to know whether a field I could not see was missing or merely unselected. It was unselected.

question: does the admin order screen show the same totals the storefront charged
answer: On this order, yes, to the cent: storefront checkout showed Subtotal 172.49 / Discount 0.00 / Tax 0.00 / Shipping 0.00 / Total 172.49, and the Admin order blade, the Admin line-items blade and GET /api/order/customerOrders all show the same. The disagreements I found are elsewhere -- the Admin operations tree renders the PaymentIn as 172.49 USD while the Admin's own Payment subtotal on the same screen renders 0.00, because the payment object holds sum=172.49 and total=0 and the two widgets read different fields; and the Shipment row renders '-' where the shipment total is 0.
found_via: placed the order and compared the storefront checkout, the Admin blades and GET /api/order/customerOrders field by field
note: The base served KB-4982C91F first -- an entry about a discount stored twice at different precision, written by a promotions run. It is adjacent, not an answer: my order carries no discount, so its claim is not observable here and I can neither confirm nor dispute it. It was still worth reading, because it names the failure SHAPE -- one quantity held twice at different precision and both rendered on one blade -- and the disagreement I did find is that shape exactly, on the payment rather than the discount. The second entry served (KB-FA724D31, deleting a member) was simply irrelevant.

question: how does a percentage reward land on the money fields of a customer order
answer: KB-FF7E4D5B says a percentage-off-cart-subtotal reward lands as exactly one entry in the ORDER-level discounts collection, with every line item keeping its full placedPrice and zero discountAmount/discountTotal, and subTotalDiscount 0. I asked it to check my own entries did not contradict a neighbour filed on the same coordinate, not to act on it. It does not contradict them, and I could not test it: no promotion applied to my order, so all of those fields were 0 for the trivial reason.
note: Asked during the consolidate read, to check the group that my four new order entries had just joined. That is the use: not the claim, the disagreement check.

question: what shape does a chosen configuration take on an order line item
answer: OrderConfigurationItemType is {id, name, type ('Product'|'Text'|'File'), customText, files} -- five fields. The cart's CartConfigurationItemType has those plus productId, quantity and sectionId, so a configuration that reaches an order keeps the chosen option's name and loses which product it was, how many, and which section it answered. Captured as KB-360127D0.
found_via: the base's own derived type tables for OrderConfigurationItemType and CartConfigurationItemType, read side by side
note: deliver served my own new entry plus the whole OrderLineItemType table -- it answered 'what is on the line item' rather than 'what is inside configurationItems'. The right table was in the derived plane all along; I had to open the file directly to get it. The retrieval, not the corpus, was the gap.
